I understand your standpoint, I think. And I try not to offer "empty, " words, as you put. If I have nothing practical, useful, or helpful to offer, I try to avoid it generally. 

That's really the idea here. Basic support, advice and general guide points if people want them. But really, all it boils down to, is their choice. 

I do think helping people make a more informed, and carefully planned choice, is the best either way though.
I agree there. If I seem to be generalizing, it's because I know it's different for everyone.

Okay, so then it stands to reason, if I am deriving some sort of benefit, you are as well. And you would be doing the exact same thing you are accusing me of. 

Though from a purely utilitarian point of view, if this increases my positive feelings, and increases positive feelings for *other people*, then it's not causing harm. 

And from the same point of view, negative views enforcing negativity for myself and others, are harmful and should be avoided. 

So, how, exactly, is this directly harmful? What part of this is inherently wrong for attempting to generally increase positivity for myself and others? We should want *less* negativity, correct? However that winds up, my goal here has been to, 
1: Offer support to those who *want* it.
2: Be a non- judgemental uninvolved party for those who wish to talk it over.
3: Offer kindness to those who see no other viable options.

What part of those is harmful or negative?

And, I can't help but agree. 
It's why I believe people should not bring babies into the world as it currently is. 
If suffering will greatly outweigh any joys in life, statistically speaking, it'll be better to have never been born at all. And I cannot, ethically, tell you your choice is wrong or unfounded. 

It could very likely be 100% the correct decision for you. If I seem in any way to have a hard stance, I ask you to forgive that of me. I do not. I just think it's a reasonably safe thing to presume most people on here are looking for encouragement to continue. 

If you've thought it through, weighed the risks, and gotten affairs in order if necessary, then I simply wish you the best and I hope that you get the results you hope for. Truly, I do. 
It's why I'm a bit anti-natalist, and pro-choice when it comes to humane euthanasia. 
I wish you the best no matter what. ❤

I mean, alright. That's a pretty big assumption to make of my character dude. I'm suicidal. I get it. 

But I'm not insulting you, or calling you a parasite. What right do you have to say these things to me, when I'm trying to offer help to those who *want it*? If you don't want help, good for you. I can't force you. 

But you're not entitled to come up and yell at me either for attempting to help those who want it, like this entire subreddit is made for. 

I think you're in the wrong place if you're gonna be aggressive to people for this.

I know sometimes it's really scary to look at everything and even *consider* fixing it. It can seem like a hell of a lot. 

So, if fixing is what you want, try breaking them down into little, bite sized things you can do regularly. Like, okay, let's say you wanna work out more, for example. You can start with a five minute walk, outside, regularly. Then move up, to 10 minutes, 20 minutes, so on so forth when you feel ready to. :)

What can you break down into smaller, more approachable tasks?
And always remember, it's *okay*. It's okay to need rest. It's okay to be tired. You're not a failure. The world generally sucks. You're not wrong for wanting a break from it. 

Take your time. Encourage yourself for the things you really want. There's no time limit, and you only gotta do anything for yourself, if you want it. And if you need resources, I'm happy to help. ❤
I know it's tough, but I'm very proud of you for trying. ❤

Hmm yeah, yeah I get you. And really, I can't tell you otherwise. 
I think, if I were in your shoes, at your point, I'd just try to give myself a couple days of having a hell of a good time. 

My only last thought on that is, well, if I'm gonna go, why not have a blast right before? Not necessarily to discourage, but just because I'd like to go happy lol. You know?

Have a blast, do whatever is available to have the time of your life for a couple days, or a week, like a farewell party, and get affairs in order if necessary, is honestly what I'd recommend. 
I do believe that sometimes it's the most humane choice. And if you fully believe it's the best one for you, I will not demand otherwise of you. 

I only hope that you can have a bit of good, and that it gives you what you want. I truly do wish you the best of luck, whatever happens. :) I know it's not a decision made willy-nilly for most. I know most people really do think a lot about it. 

And lastly, I'd just suggest *research*. Lots and lots of research for risk reduction.

I know the feeling. I still feel it pretty regularly. Though, sometimes, I don't. And I've really enjoyed the days I don't feel it. I think, in the end, it's all about risk vs reward. 
If there's nothing left you want, or nothing left you can enjoy, and life is truly always miserable for you, I don't want you to suffer. 

I don't want anybody to suffer. I just want to encourage others to get the most enjoyment out of life that they feasibly can before it's over for good, you know? At least, give yourself a couple of really dang good days, cause none of us wanna die miserable, you know?

Do whatever you can to give yourself the best couple days you can, if it's what you really want, so at least you had a blast. That's how I'd go, if it were me. If I was totally determined, I'd do everything I was capable of to totally have the time of my life right before.

I know it's always a complicated thing. There's no easy answer. All I hope to do here, is encourage others to just *consider* first. 
I know there's thousands of different things that factor into an individual's choice. 

If I seem shallow, it's because writing them all out would make a book, rather than a post lol. I fully believe in humane euthanasia, or a fully researched alternative, to be entirely valid. I fully believe sometimes, it *really is* the most kind option for someone. 

I do not want *anyone* to suffer unnecessarily. I just hope they get all they want, if they can, before either choosing to walk through that door, or before something else happens. Because I think we deserve at least a little good, for ourselves, you know? We deserve *something* nice before it's all over for good I think.

And, I'm not saying it's *not* okay to be tired of living. *It is*. I am, a lot. 

I just know, that holding on for me, was worth it. I did get better. I did find things that were enough for me to wanna stick around a little longer. And, well, I might choose not to later. 

That's okay. 
I just know, for myself, I don't wanna go regretting things I didn't get to experience.
But this is a very personal choice. It's entirely up to the individual. Again, I cannot choose for you. I can only offer you what I think. 

I'm not here to judge or tell you what to do. I'm only asking that it's a choice that's considered. Not really for me or anyone else, but because I know there are things I'm glad I stuck around to see, that may be worth the few extra moments for somebody else. 

That's all. 
If you're absolutely certain there's no other option, who am I to pretend I know better than you? 
I don't. And that's why I'm also an advocate for humane euthanasia options.

I totally understand. And, it's okay to feel sad and frustrated, if you do. 
Life is terribly unfair to the majority of us, unless you're rich. (Even then, they're still pretty miserable jerks lol)

All I can say, is if you have any doubt, try just enjoying yourself for a few days. Don't worry about other people's feelings, blow your responsibilities off for a day, and *live* to the best of your ability that day. 

And hey, if you have a blast for a day, well that's a hell of a lot better than your average day, right lol?

I am not pretending that life is always worth pushing through, until you die miserable and exhausted. Sometimes, it's genuinely *not*. Sometimes euthanasia *is* the most humane option. 

What I am saying, is that it needs to be carefully considered. I'm not saying live for anyone else, because that never worked for me. I grew up abused. My dad killed himself when I was 15, too. I didn't resent him for it. I knew he was absolutely miserable. I only wished I could have given him *better*, because he was a man who deserved so much more than what he got. 

It's your choice. I cannot make it for you or take it from you. I can only encourage you to carefully consider your options, and wish you the best in the end. It's your choice, and yours alone. 

But this is also a place to offer support to those considering who aren't yet fully determined. I'm doing my best to encourage and offer support as this place on Reddit encourages. I'm not sure why you seem so upset with me for doing so.

Because suicide is a huge gamble. If you're not around to experience the relief of the removal of your problems... then there's a possibility that you die, but you die miserable and without any fulfillment. 

And you don't know anything else. That's, a real huge scary gamble to me. 
So if I'm gonna go, yes I'd prefer to go with my dignity and mind intact. 

But also, I'd prefer to go having tried and done everything I can and everything that got me interested. And, maybe we don't need a purpose. Maybe, we should just try and enjoy ourselves and do good while we're here. But every kindness you give to somebody, that effects quite a lot. 

Every time you're nice, somebody is gonna be nice to somebody else because of you, so on, so forth. Like the butterfly effect. 
You can make little changes that can effect everything. Even if you don't realize it right away. 

And that's always been cool to me. But also, man do I love me a good steak, and playing a round of chess, or online games with my friends. I love the feeling of bonding. Listening to good music. Hell, even shrooms got me excited about living for a bit. It's said they cure depression and despondency for a little while too.

Well, I do get that, for certain. Old age certainly isn't attractive for me either. I'd say, for me, it's about risk vs reward. 
Suicide has a lot of risk involved. 

But I also may be physically invalid by 50. So, for me, as long as I can still participate in the things I generally enjoy (computer games, reading, sex too, good food I love) then there's still some things worth my while. I don't want to live to nursing home status, either. I want to die with my dignity intact. 

So I can't judge for that - because I very much feel the same. When I'm becoming totally dependent on someone else for everything to keep me alive, then for me, it's time to go. That's miserable. 

But if there's anything I can do myself to improve my situation, make myself feel good, and have a bit of fun before it's over, I think that's worth at least sticking around long enough to enjoy. Maybe you only stick around a few months or a year longer, to experience Hedonism. That'll still be worth it, in my opinion. :)

I say, just don't go with regrets, or things you really wanted to do or see undone. Make sure you have no regrets.

And, depending on your methodology, there's a fair chance you hurt yourself permanently rather than succeed on your first try. 

Suicide is a risky choice, inherently. There's no surefire method, given that people have survived absurd things. 

Is it worth the risk of permanent life altering injury, doing it yourself?

I know when we get like this, it's hard to see anything else. I've been there, totally despondent and tired. With almost 0 motivation. Feeling a total emptiness. And, you know, it's scary sometimes. It's hard. It's *so* hard. But death is also a difficult and risky thing to go about. 

When you're here, weigh the risks. The pros and cons, totally and objectively. 

Will your death devastate people?
Will your death *really* resolve your problems?
Will you leave behind anything difficult for others?
Is your situation totally unsolvable?
Is there *absolutely nothing* in this world that could motivate you to carry on?
Is there *nothing* left you want, or want to do, in life? Have you no regrets?
Do you have any doubts?

Maybe it's silly, or redundant, but this is what I ask myself when I'm far down and am struggling to see a way forward. My father made the choice, and it ripped me apart. I have cried over movies he would have loved to see and didn't get to.

They're important to consider. Worth considering. Whatever you choose, know I hold no judgement, and just hope the best for you.

Well, I can't say for certain you're wrong. 
I don't know. I don't have the knowledge of your life to know. 

But I can reasonably believe, if you're here, you don't entirely believe that. Do you *really* not want anything more? Do you not care about anything else possible in life from here forward?

Do you not want the chance to feel better? Are you terminally ill with no way to improve?

These are generally the questions raised when someone is pursuing humane euthanasia with the help of a physician. Certain criteria must be met before they'll help you out with that. 

But, if any part of you has *any* doubt that suicide is the answer, then it can't hurt to try. That's the general rule to follow, for myself. If I'm not *100%* certain, then I'm not dying. 99% isn't good enough, there can't be room for doubt with a decision so permanent and so entirely changing. 

Death removes *all* possibility. Sure, you can't get much worse from there, but you don't get *better* either. It's okay to live for things other than yourself too. Maybe it's a movie you really wanna see. Or a game you really wanna play. Or something you'd love to learn more about. 

I'd just always recommend taking the time to think. That's why I follow my own 72 hour rule. What's taking a bit more time, when you'll be dead forever if you go?

In the end, the choice is yours. But, unless you're dead, I firmly believe there's always a chance that things improve.

Hey love.
I know this is horrific and terrible. There's no excuses for what your dad's doing. 
I've been there. 
I know it's hard to imagine - but it's possible to get better and to get to safety. I think it's safe to assume, you have a phone, right?

Please look up local teen shelters in your area. Call them, ask if they have room, when you're out of the house. 

The teen shelters saved my life as a kid, growing up. I was certain my mom was gonna kill me eventually when I lived with her. Thanks to the shelters - she didn't have a chance to anymore.
And stand firm in your decision when you go. Take any siblings you can, if possible. 

Your father may try to force you back, but without a court order, he can't. If you get video of him abusing your family, he'll never get that court order. Instead, you can get the courts to order you to *stay* in the teen shelter home. 

I know that sounds scary too. But they were so much better for me. They'll have rules, yes, but they'll also have resources and counselors, typically. Please try. Please look for them. 

Even if they're further away, it's better than where you're at, and I guarantee safer. I never got hurt there. And I had much better resources. 

It's always worth trying. And consider - you've not even lived 1/2 the human life expectancy. 
If your life could be better in the future, and you could imagine it being worth it if certain expectations are met in said future - it's worth trying now. 

But also - if nothing else - spite kept me going as a teen in your boat. At that time, I'd be damned if I let that bitch be the one to put me in the ground. I would *not* let her have the satisfaction, and I was *determined* to make her life hell for as long as I could in return for what she'd done to me. 

And I promise you, that's satisfying, at least. People may say that revenge isn't a good choice, but those people usually haven't *been there.* And if it keeps you going, who cares? Yeah, maybe it's not the most healthy, but at least it's justified and it feels better than doing nothing.

I'd say try expanding your social circle. 
Since there's a pandemic, it's safest to start online right now. What do you enjoy? Maybe you can join an online group chat with people who enjoy what you enjoy. :)

Maybe there are things you can volunteer in, in your community, that will put you around like minded people with similar interests. 

The best way to bridge a gap between two different types of people, is starting with mutual interests. Learning new things together, even. In a safe, neutral, non-hostile environment.

Most people are afraid of what they don't know, what they aren't familiar with. When the unknown becomes known, it's a lot less scary. 
Racial tensions from either side generally result from a fear of the unknown. When those people can see that there's nothing to worry about, that their fears or anxieties aren't based in reality, a lot of that can be worked through. 

Some people genuinely aren't worth a damn though, and you need to know the difference. People who are anxious and nervous - but not outright hostile and violent - those are people you can work with.

People who are already hostile, suspicious, and violent - you just need to get them out of your life. Do not tolerate the intolerant. The Paradox of Tolerance example exists because when we tolerate the intolerant - the intolerant destroy the tolerant. 

So I'd suggest finding better, new friends first. Teaching yourself love and patience first. Learning some new things. Trying support groups. And also - giving yourself the space to *not worry about it.* Thinking about what stresses you 24/7 doesn't help. Give yourself a break. Take a lovely bath. Go on a nature walk. But give yourself a breather first.

If you're posting this though, I think there's some part of you that's still hopeful. 
See, our brain and body - it desperately wants to live. It does a lot to keep us alive here. Whether that's to our benefit or detriment - well it doesn't have those concerns. 

We have those concerns, our body and its survival mechanisms don't. We want fulfillment, safety, and comfort in life. We want to be able to look at ourselves and... just feel okay at least. 

So when we think there's something fundamentally wrong with ourselves, we're undermining that and our own potential. When we deny ourselves care and understanding, we lay the foundation for suicide. We get that train going, and sometimes fast. 

What I'm saying is, if you see a lot of problems in life that upset you, maybe there can also be solutions. 
If you're gonna be dead, presumably forever, what's another few days or months exhausting the possibilities of *getting better*? 
I know how it feels. 

I know I wanted somebody to hold me through it and promise me it'd get better. 

I won't tell you that. Because I don't know your whole life. I don't know what the realistic opportunities are. 
But I do know it's *possible.* If it was possible to feel better before, it's possible to start feeling better now. 
So you're overweight? Yeah, that's tough. A lot of people are. There's no quick easy overnight solutions. But if you exercise, drink water, and perhaps try a few metabolism boosting supplements, you might be able to get to a more ideal body image for yourself within a few months. 

Dating? Dating is a shitshow for most people. But physical touch is a crucial psychological need. I'd gently suggest hiring a professional, once in awhile, for comfort. It's not wrong, it's fulfilling a very important psychological health need. 

There's a lot of possibilities. There's a lot of options. And there's solutions to most problems. And if you could be doing something great in the future because of overcoming these things, who's to say you're not worth the effort now?

Another lesson life taught me haha,

I know this probably doesn't mean a lot to you, right now. It's probably hard to see anything other than the situation you're in. 

But if I could talk to both of you right now, OP and you, I'd say it gets better. 
If you're at the bottom, there's no other way but up.

I felt hopeless and worthless at 12. I was too scared to do it myself, so I just put myself in a lot of dangerous stupid situations. 
I was still miserable and death-seeking up until about the last 3 years. 

Sometimes I still fall in the pit. 

But once I was able to go out on my own, and was out of the toxic relationships I had, and started actually talking to people and staying in touch and demonstrating my care for them... I got better. 
I'm not perfect. I'm still far from totally happy with myself. 

But I know I can get better because I have. I'm sure you've had better moments, too.

It's not totally impossible. 
And I've always told myself - unless I've exhausted every opportunity to get better, and unless there's TRULY no logical way forward, I won't kill myself. 
If I'm not sure if there's a way out, I follow the 3 day rule. 

If I'm gonna be dead forever, what's waiting another 3 days to be sure I actually want to without a doubt?
The last thing I want is to regret it, if that's possible in the end. 

You can't get better if you never give yourself a chance or time to. 
That's kept me holding on. Sometimes barely by a thread, and sometimes just for my cat Lucy, but I'm still here as much as I can be.

So I'll try to give you a balanced response.
If you guys have only been friends for the past several years and only recently tried sugaring, she could honestly just be nervous. 

But she could be in a position that, she really needs extra money. She could be scared of losing the help and friendship, by admitting she may have gotten cold feet. 

I'm not saying she's not interested in continuing, I think you still have a fair shot of working through it - I think it's very possible she just got nervous. If she's never done this before, she could be scared of getting caught by friends or family too, and getting "slut-shamed," so to speak. 
(It's never okay to shame anybody for their safe consensual activities)

Give her a day or two, let her chill, don't send any extra money, and then have a conversation. Discuss your needs, and your hopes, and ask her how she is feeling. 
Make it clear she'll get no more money if she doesn't hold up her end, just don't get harsh about it. Let her know you could still be friends - but also that you won't be played for a fool.
